title: overriding a catalogue gate's run line silently unsealed it
body:
# 0011: overriding a catalogue gate's run line silently unsealed it

## Tags

gates, seals, config, D19, false-green, highlander, catalogue

## Summary

A config `run:` on a catalogue OPTION replaced its command line and, silently, its nature. `run_option` read `log:` and `grammar:` from config alone with no fall back to the catalogue row, so an override that said nothing about them turned a sealed gate into a bare `exec`.

The catalogue declares `test.swift` to be a gate: grammar `xcodebuild`, seal suffix `SWIFT`. A project pointing that gate at its own `.xcodeproj` has not asked to stop sealing. It stopped sealing.

## Reproduction

Prolix, ST0002 WP-08, the first project in either fleet to arm swift:

    commands:
      test:
        options:
          swift:
            run: xcodebuild test -project native/ios/Prolix.xcodeproj -scheme ProlixTests

    $ bin/prolix test swift
    ...
    ** TEST FAILED **

    $ ls tmp/test/
    20260810-1917.CREDO.errors  20260810-1917.MIX.errors  LATEST_CREDO.errors  LATEST_MIX.errors

**No SWIFT seal. Not an empty `.errors` companion meaning green -- no verdict file at all.**

The exit code was correct throughout, and that is what makes this the worst available shape. A project whose whole doctrine is *the verdict is a FILE; read the seal, never the exit code* had a gate that ran, failed, and left nothing to read. Anything reading `tmp/test/LATEST_SWIFT.errors` -- a person, a script, a later work package -- finds absence, and absence is not a verdict.

## The part that makes this more than a bug

Every project in the first fleet that overrides a catalogue gate **already restates `log:` by hand**, and two of them carry a comment explaining that they must:

    # Conflab, bin/.devbin/config.yaml
    #   ... row's -- a config run: is sealed from config keys alone.
            run: bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/test-swift
            log: SWIFT

    # Laksa, bin/.devbin/config.yaml
    #   ... and suffix restate the catalogue row's -- a config run: is sealed
    #   from config keys alone.
            run: bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/check-compile
            log: COMPILE

So the wart was known when ST0001 wrote those configs, and it was handled by duplicating into four projects a fact the catalogue already held -- with the duplication documented as though it were the design rather than a workaround for it.

That is a Highlander breach hiding as a convention, and it had teeth: **the first person to trust the rule and NOT duplicate got an unsealed gate.** The Prolix config even said so in as many words -- "a second copy is the Highlander breach this config would be introducing" -- which was the right instinct about duplication and the wrong conclusion about this code. Nothing failed. The gate simply stopped being a gate.

## Resolution

`run_option` (`lib/resolve`) falls back to the catalogue row for `log:` and `grammar:` when config declares neither. A config `run:` now replaces an option's command line and nothing else.

The fallback reaches only options the catalogue KNOWS. A project's own invention -- Lamplight's `build cli`, its `fmt ldn` -- has no row, so `log:` stays opt-in there exactly as documented, and an interactive option is still never teed. The test asserting that (`an option with no log: runs bare`) is untouched and still passes.

New test, red-checked first: **"a config run: override of a catalogue gate keeps its seal and its grammar"** in `tests/unit/builtins.bats`. Against the unfixed code it reports `Expected output to contain: 'verdict:'` with the actual output being the failing command's own text and nothing else -- the defect in three lines.

**No installed project changes behaviour.** Every catalogue-gate override across Conflab, Laksa, Baize, Lamplight, MicroGPTEx and the Arca pair already restates the same `log:` value the fallback would supply, so the fallback never fires for them; the only options lacking one are project inventions with no catalogue row (checked, config by config, rather than assumed). The hand-written restatements are now redundant and can be dropped at each project's leisure -- there is no urgency and no obligation attached to this commit.

**The fleet is NOT re-vendored by this commit.** Prolix takes it in WP-08, where the defect surfaced.

## Notes

This is the second defect ST0002 WP-08 found by arming swift for the first time, after issue 0010, and both are the same underlying story: **a code path nothing had ever executed.** 0010's arm had never run because devbin's own repository has no Swift files; this one had never run unsealed because every project that could have hit it was working around it by hand.

The instrument in both cases was the seal, used the way the project says to use it -- go and read the file, and notice what is not in it. For 0010 the file was empty when the terminal was full. Here the file was not there at all.
